raw_text:
This is nonsevere unilateral acute otitis media (bulging TM plus effusion and acute otalgia), without otorrhea or complications.

I would offer watchful waiting with reliable 48–72-hour follow-up as the preferred plan, using shared decision-making. At exactly 24 months, with mild otalgia for <48 hours and temperature <39°C, either observation or immediate antibiotics is guideline-concordant. AAP guideline

Pain/fever:

Acetaminophen 15 mg/kg/dose PO q4–6h PRN: 186 mg/dose; if 160 mg/5 mL, give 5.8 mL (practically 6 mL).

Or ibuprofen 10 mg/kg/dose PO q6–8h PRN: 124 mg/dose; if 100 mg/5 mL, give 6.2 mL. Avoid if dehydrated or unable to maintain intake. Ibuprofen labeling

Fluids and comfort care. No decongestants, antihistamines, or OTC cough/cold products for the ear infection.

No labs or imaging indicated today.

Provide a delayed (“safety-net”) prescription or arrange prompt reassessment if pain/fever worsens at any time or is not clearly improving by 48–72 hours:

Amoxicillin 90 mg/kg/day divided BID × 7 days

For 12.4 kg: 560 mg PO BID (e.g., amoxicillin 400 mg/5 mL: 7 mL BID).

Escalate urgently for postauricular swelling/erythema or ear displacement, persistent high fever/toxic appearance, dehydration, severe headache/neurologic symptoms, or new otorrhea. Persistent middle-ear effusion alone after clinical recovery does not require treatment.
